name: AFM level 2 task 9: Friction Repeatability And Surface-Check Measurement
description: Acquire exactly three consecutive contact-mode lateral-force images of the same region without changing any acquisition parameter. Use a scan size of 5 µm × 5 µm, resolution of 256 × 256 pixels, time per line of 0.075 s, normal-force setpoint of 10 nN, and P/I/D gains of 100/50/0. For every acquisition, calculate average friction magnitude and its spatial standard deviation from the lateral channels, and Ra and Rq from the height channel. Across the three acquisitions, report the mean, sample standard deviation, and coefficient of variation of average friction, Ra, and Rq. Use changes in the height images only to flag possible surface modification; do not claim wear without independent evidence. Save each completed acquisition as a distinct raw .nid file and report its absolute path. Submit images in acquisition order with recorded_params and physical_settings as numeric objects using the benchmark units. Centers are relative to the initial scan center, in nm. Record the complete acquisition state for every image. Common roughness rules: use the full forward height channel in meters; subtract a least-squares plane, then its residual mean, without filtering, masking or line flattening. Ra is mean absolute residual and Rq is RMS residual; report both in nm. Common friction rules: record height and lateral trace/retrace channels. Supply channels as NSFopen channel-name mappings (topography, lateral_trace, lateral_retrace) and retrace_reversed as a boolean indicating whether retrace columns need reversing to align physical coordinates. Use lateral signals in V; friction map = abs((trace - aligned retrace)/2). Report its mean and population spatial standard deviation in V. Do not claim calibrated force or a friction coefficient from voltage data. Aggregate standard deviations use ddof=1; CV is 100 * sample standard deviation / mean. Percentage changes are 100 * (value - reference) / reference. Use null for undefined ratios or R².
